title: No sense of esthetics
author: Fresh_Criticism6531
selftext:
Hi, I am vibe coding a game, I have tons of claude tokens to play with, and to me it looks like claude has no sense of esthetics. It will happily make very ugly ui elements, draw 5 lines in a svg with python and say this is a plane, etc.

Any way to work around this? Maybe generate stuff with image generators and tell claude to use that as inspiration to make the UI?

How to make the man get a grip on esthetics?

I personally am not a designer, so I don't know what exactly I want, but definetively not what he is doing.

I am baffled by how good he codes and how bad he makes designs. Seems I must be doing something wrong, as I previously hard AI was hitting graphical designers badly, even before it started hitting programmers badly.

Maybe my tools suck? Maybe I should give up on 2D and go 3D?

ideas?

Unfortunately I don't have tokens in any other model, just the 3 free daily images from chatgpt, but I am planning on buying a laptop with GeForce and try to run an image model there...

comments.author: Prior-Requirement-40
comments.body:
As far as models go, from what I've notice ChatGPT handles UI the best, Google handles concept art the best and Claude handles the code/implementation the best. I'm about a week into making an indie game that is intended for both PC and phones, and the UI mockup ChatGPT did was honestly gorgeous, but Claude's implementation looks like a Flash game at best.

After a week of refining (graphics still feel like a decent alpha state), what I learned was to just keep feeding it references, restating exactly what you are looking for, saving every design idea as a plan or rules, and working alongside Claude as its actual pair of eyes.

Even then, I've spent hours refining small details, reiterating upon the game's consistent style, finding new tools/workflows, etc., it's all a huge work in progress still. I think you just have to treat it as if you were making the game yourself: it will start out as an ugly prototype, but both you and Claude will learn more about your game and making games over time, and the finished product will begin to come together over time like you were making a painting.

replies.author: Fresh_Criticism6531
replies.body:
What does your graphics pipeline look like?

Your game is 3D or 2D?

replies.author: Prior-Requirement-40
replies.body:
Game is 2.5D, meant to be a Nintendo inspired side scroller/beat-em up with cel-shaded art. 3D characters and models, etc. Honestly part of why I chose it was because I wanted to see how far I could get with Claude from a style pov

I wish I had a more concrete answer for you, I just finished burning all my tokens creating plans for a huge graphics overhaul to get it to a state im more happy with. I can tell you my progression at least

Nano Banana and ChatGPT for concept art and UI design respectively, after lots of reference material and discussion with them and Claude. The concept art was then fed to Meshy, Tripo, and Ludo for the player model. I was happiest with Ludo, Claude then recreated that horrendous model with blender-mcp

Almost all of my background assets, textures, lighting, etc. Claude currently generates procedurally or uses Godot's tools (for stuff like lighting, fog, SSAO, depth of field etc). It looks decent, a bit above flash game quality but at this point I'm trying to get beyond that

My current plan for the future is using Material Maker and ArmorPaint for textures, Blender for models, Cascadeur on a free tier for animations unless I find an alternative. All of this being done by Claude while I watch because I'm just a guy with a full time job

comments.author: Ok-Investment4414
comments.body: gotta say what kinda game u making and functionality > aesthetics if u are on a time clock since u can change the assets any time

replies.author: Fresh_Criticism6531
replies.body:
I'm making a space 4x game.

I just asked him to switch to raw OpenGL and installed Blender. Looks definetively better.

replies.author: Ok-Investment4414
replies.body: it works best for blender with concept images , measurements and assembling as parts vs an entire thing gpt can get u those images broken down for assemble. Once that good u can look for free mats and textures or make your own. Then its wise to make an assembler so for instance in your case a planet generator or a spaceship generator save u time and tokens

comments.author: Unturned1
comments.body: Claude can make amazing art, it just can't start from nothing. There is a bigger problem which is you can't ask it to do what you want because you do not understand what you want and how it is suppose to look. Saying make it look good is not a vision.

replies.author: Harlan_42
replies.body: Does that make the answer to ask Claude to learn the skill, or teach the skill so the prompter knows what to ask for when wanting them?

replies.author: Unturned1
replies.body:
This problem does not have a solution in this sense.

The solution is to look at some art, take a few art classes, look at beautiful things, write about what makes them beautiful.

Develop an understanding of what you like and why you like it.

replies.author: Fresh_Criticism6531
replies.body:
Well, I don't think I gave him nothing. I gave tons of screenshots of similar games and wanted "something similar". But the result was atrocious.

I was never good with graphics.

Basically I'm kind of surprized by the disconect here. When it comes to coding, he is the king. I didn't look at a single line of code, and the whole thing works. Well, the whole game structure already existed, its not from zero, but I had stopped it because coding it is too much effort time-wise and wasn't worth it. But with claude now the project can be done. I don't even actually have to make requirements, I can ask him for requirements based on similar games. Sure there is a initial vision I had, but it actually already surpassed it by far.

And then when it comes to graphics, basically nothing he did satisfies me, nothing he did is good enough for a final version at all. Its all comparable with a 80's game in his best moments, 1970's in the worse.

And I gave many examples of similar stuff. I also tried to make him write prompts for DALL-E, but I have to iterate too many times on DALL-E, its also hard, and its 2D anyway, I'm moving to 3D.

 "Claude can make amazing art"

How exactly? Doing which pipeline exactly? I heard I should ask him to make a python script to generate a model in Blender? That's the way?

His pixel-by-pixel art is atrocious.

replies.author: Unturned1
replies.body:
I don't want to sound flippant because I can see that you are trying, but you need to figure out first of all what you are going for and why it isn't matching what you had in mind. Verbalizing those details and working on getting them right consistently is literally what artists do beyond simply the mechanical skill placing ink on a page. There are beautiful games from the 80s and 70s and no so much so. You're inability to create a workflow that satisfies your requirements is quite literally a skill issue, not a claude skill issue, your skill issue. Nothing says you can't get help, or develop the skill yourself but the tool is just that a tool.

If it has already surpassed what you had in mind, why don't you go back and make the simple version of what you wanted?

comments.author: Ai_Test_4704
comments.body: not one AI can handle anything regarding UI if not instructed with a 1000 words novel. I'm making a really small mobile game, 2D, super simply... I change one screen and without any warnings, codex changed the other half and messed the up the layouts. And the best part... it can't be undone, I'm not using git and codex can't undo the changes because he's behaving like he has alzheimer.

replies.author: Fresh_Criticism6531
replies.body:
yeah, I faced the same problem regarding UI.... 

But you should really be using git, there is no reason not to (actually my game is in subversion, but that an old legacy version control system). I think you can even ask AI to make a local-only repo and then you commit every once a day even.

And anyway, isn't AI great at reverting previous work? I didn't really use the version control much besides as a "backup"

comments.author: Harlan_42
comments.body: Find a game development platform that will make graphics with a free account.  Ask Claude where to find free graphics you can use in your game.  Sign up for Adobe Photoshop for the free week and use it to generate images.  Use Claude as the clearing house to arrange and place the images and maybe some page decoration.

comments.body:
